summary: 1941 Plumas NF lookout that replaced a 1933-34 station; staffed in the 1950s and 60s; a 2026 Forest Service renovation is out for quotes.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on an enclosed timber tower, per the register
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Plumas National Forest

events.note: Replaced a lookout the register dates to 1933 or 1934
New station to be built by a CCC spike camp (June 6, 1941 report), to be finished by June 30
A fire set by a hunter who thought he was lost, in September 1949, was spotted by the Red Rock lookout
Wanda Hansen (also spelled Hanson) named as the lookout; the family staffed it into the early 1960s
Forest Service RFQ 127EAW26Q0028 for deferred-maintenance renovation; responses due October 21, 2026; Amendment 03 (August 27, 2026) added site-visit information

notes_for_editor: No source found on current staffing, public access, or whether the cab is open to visitors, so those keys are omitted. The newspaper staffing items end in 1962. Sources spell the lookout staffer both Hansen and Hanson. The register's earlier 1933/34 lookout is not confirmed by the newspaper items I read. The register's photo credit (2008, Ron Kemnow) has no image URL, so no photos are recorded. The GovTribe copies of the RFQ attachments returned HTTP 403; the story relies on the FBO Daily notice. The FBO notice's Amendment 05 (October 1, 2026) changed the quote due date; the story uses the response date shown on the notice. No corrections to the record: the 1941 build year, agency and elevation match the register.
